title: The 9/21 EMA cross that took a $50k ES account to $449 on 5 minute candles finished up 32% on 15 minute
author: person-person12
selftext:
I ran the 9/21 EMA cross on 5 minute ES recently and it took a $50k account down to $449 between January 2021 and July 2024. I wanted to know how much of that was the strategy and how much was the 5 minute chart, so I ran the exact same rules in [Agenticks](https://www.agenticks.ca/?utm_source=reddit&utm_medium=post&utm_campaign=autopilot&utm_content=ai_trading) on 15 minute ES candles over the same window, one contract, with commission and slippage charged on every fill.

**15 minute ES, Jan 2021 to Jul 2024, $50k start:**

* 892 trades
* 40% win rate
* profit factor 1.05
* **net +$16,247, about 32%**
* max drawdown 31%
* $15,610 in trading costs

**5 minute ES, same rules, same window:**

* 1,981 trades
* 35% win rate
* profit factor 0.91
* **net -$49,551**
* $34,668 in trading costs

On 5 minute the signal itself was down about $15k before costs and fees took another $35k on top of that. On 15 minute the same rules were up roughly $32k before costs and fees took about half of it back. The timeframe **cut the trade count by more than half** and that alone is most of the gap between blowing the account and finishing green.

32% over three and a half years with a 31% drawdown still isnt something id take near a prop eval tbh, because a 31% drop on $50k is about $15k and a 50k eval usually stops you out long before that. The curve also did almost all of its work in early 2022 while ES was trending down hard, going from about $56k in January to $78k by late April, and spent most of the two years after that going sideways between $55k and $67k.

comments.author: filwu
comments.body: That 15-minute result still looks regime-sensitive: you note most gains came in early 2022 and the curve then went sideways. Since the tested window ends July 2024, a clean next check would freeze the 9/21 rule and costs, then report an untouched post-July-2024 period plus rolling yearly returns and drawdowns against a simple trend or buy-and-hold baseline. With PF 1.05 after costs, showing whether the edge survives that split matters more than the headline +32%.

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: Yea you called it, so I froze the same rules and costs and ran 15 minute ES from August 2024 to this week, none of which it had seen before. 541 trades, 38% winners, profit factor 0.95, and the $50k finished at $37,399, which is **down 25% with a 44% drawdown** on the way. Costs were about $9,500 of that and gross it was down roughly 6%, so the 32% was mostly early 2022 doing the work.

comments.author: Only-Assignment3982
comments.body: Going from almost blowing the $50k account to finishing up 32% just by changing timeframes is pretty crazy. But a 1.05 profit factor and 31% drawdown still wouldn't make me comfortable. I use Moon for shorter market wagers, and this really highlights why trade frequency and costs deserve as much attention as the entry signal itself.

replies.author: person-person12
replies.body: Yea I wouldnt run it either, a 1.05 profit factor is close enough to breakeven that a couple of bad months wipe it out, and **31% down on $50k** is about $15.5k gone at the worst point. The only thing that changed between the two runs was the candle size, same cross and same rules.

comments.author: QATSAlgo
comments.body:
The prop comparison is the key point: the relevant test is whether the strategy survives the account’s loss floor along the whole path, not whether it ends above $50k. I’d replay the exact daily reset and trailing/EOD rule before interpreting either curve as an evaluation candidate. A thin 1.05 profit factor also deserves cost-sensitivity checks on a period not used to choose the timeframe.
